title: The CEO Who Ordered a Hit on His Own Factory to Collect Insurance
hook: When profits fell, this executive didn't restructure — he burned everything down and blamed an immigrant worker.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends true crime and business — viewers love stories of rich people destroying lives for money.

title: The Trader Who Crashed His Own Bank with a Secret Algorithm
hook: He coded a script that siphoned micro-pennies from millions of trades — until the system collapsed.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-tech heist narrative appeals to both finance and tech audiences.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI' — It Was 300 Minimum Wage Workers in a Basement
hook: Investors thought they were funding a neural network. Instead, they were funding a sweatshop of human clickers.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'fake AI' expose triggers outrage and fascination with how easily VCs are fooled.

title: How One Company Bought Every Grocery Store in a Town to Control Prices
hook: You think inflation is natural? This corporation owned the supply chain, the shelves, and the cash register in one zip code.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable pain point (high grocery prices) with a hidden culprit triggers shareability.

title: The Spy Who Got a Job Just to Dump Coffee on a Laptop
hook: A rival company paid an operative $50,000 to spill a latte on the only copy of a billion-dollar design.
why_this_can_go_viral: Low-tech sabotage with high stakes — cinematic and easy to visualize.

title: The Ads That Programmed You to Crave Salt at 3 PM
hook: Snack companies paid neuroscientists to find your brain's weakest hour — then targeted it with precision.
why_this_can_go_viral: Viewers love feeling 'exposed' — reveals how their own cravings are engineered.

title: The Cotton That Came From a Prison — Sold as 'Ethical'
hook: Your 'sustainable' t-shirt was picked by inmates making 12 cents an hour in a for-profit penitentiary.
why_this_can_go_viral: Moral outrage + fashion industry hypocrisy = explosive shareability.

title: The Dentist Who Knew His Fillings Were Toxic — and Sold Them for 20 Years
hook: He had the memo. He had the test results. He kept using the material because switching would cost him money.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal health betrayal angle — everyone has been to the dentist, making it highly relatable.

title: The Pharma CEO Who Dosed Himself with His Own Drug — Then Died
hook: He was so confident in the safety of his painkiller that he took it on live TV. Three days later, he was gone.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shocking, ironic, and full of dramatic tension — perfect for short-form storytelling.

title: The Algorithm That Made You Pay Double for a Flight Because You're Rich
hook: Airlines detected your credit score, your phone model, and your zip code — then raised the price by 200%.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone has felt ripped off by flight prices — this explains why it's not random.

title: The Startup That Rented a Private Island to Convince Investors It Was Successful
hook: They had zero revenue. But with a rented jet, a fake office, and paid actors, they raised $40 million.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'pretend billionaire' trope is endlessly fascinating and easy to visualize.

title: The Company That Got a Patent for the Shape of a Chair — Then Sued Everyone
hook: They didn't invent anything. They just patented a curve — and collected billions in royalties from every furniture store.
why_this_can_go_viral: Patent trolling outrage is a proven trigger for shares among creators and small business owners.

title: The Rival Who Sent a 'Repairman' to Install a Bug in the Boardroom
hook: He wasn't fixing the AC. He was planting a microphone that listened to merger talks for six months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic spy thriller in real life — high intrigue and easy to dramatize.

title: The 'Limited Edition' Scam That Made You Buy a Product That Was Never Limited
hook: They printed 'only 500 made' on the box. They made 50,000. And they knew you'd pay triple for the 'exclusivity.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals the psychological trick behind 'scarcity' — viewers love feeling smart for knowing the truth.

title: The Chocolate That Was Made with Cocoa Beans Stolen from a War Zone
hook: Your favorite Valentine's Day box was sweetened by child labor and armed militias controlling the supply route.
why_this_can_go_viral: Emotional shock + love for chocolate = massive share potential, especially around holidays.

title: The Tobacco Company That Secretly Made Its Own Ads Look Stupid
hook: They paid ad agencies to create terrible anti-smoking ads — because bad campaigns kept people smoking.
why_this_can_go_viral: Conspiracy-level revelation that feels both true and shocking — perfect for debate in comments.

title: The CEO Who Burned $100 Million on a Super Bowl Ad — Then Fled the Country
hook: He spent the company's last dime on a 30-second spot. The stock crashed the next morning. He was already in Brazil.
why_this_can_go_viral: Rags-to-riches-to-absurd-fall — high drama, easy to narrate, strong visual hook.

title: The Hedge Fund That Hired a Pilot to Fly Over a Factory — for a 3-Second Head Start
hook: One trading firm paid a private pilot to circle a cargo ship. They saw the load before the market did — and made $50 million.
why_this_can_go_viral: Sounds illegal but wasn't — 'legal cheating' triggers outrage and awe among viewers.

title: The Founder Who Ran a Startup for 5 Years Without Selling Anything
hook: He raised $30 million, hired 200 people, built an app — and never shipped a single product. No one noticed.
why_this_can_go_viral: The absurdity of 'faking it' for years is both hilarious and dark — strong anti-VC sentiment boosting shares.

title: The Company That Bought the Only Supplier of a Critical Chip — Then Raised Prices 1,000%
hook: They didn't invent the chip. They just bought the guy who made it — then charged everyone rent for years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the real-world chip shortage frustration — explains why prices are so high.

title: The Intern Who Copied the Entire Client List — and Sold It to a Rival for $2,000
hook: He was 19, paid minimum wage, and walked out with a flash drive worth $14 million to the competition.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable underpaid worker narrative + shocking betrayal = strong emotional hook.

title: The Vitamin Bottle That Contained Sawdust and Sugar — Labeled 'Organic'
hook: They spent more on the label design than the ingredients. And they sold it to health-conscious people for $60 a bottle.
why_this_can_go_viral: Health-conscious audience + betrayal of trust = outrage-driven sharing.

title: The Tire Company That Knew Its Product Exploded — and Blamed the Drivers
hook: Internal memos showed the defect was known for 7 years. They paid settlements secretly and changed the name.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic 'corporation vs. consumer' narrative with life-and-death stakes.

title: The Facebook Ads That Targeted You Based on Your Ex's Location
hook: A marketing agency scraped breakup data from social media — then sold you products you'd only buy when heartbroken.
why_this_can_go_viral: Hyper-personal, creepy, and relatable — everyone knows someone going through a breakup.

title: The Company That Paid You to 'Review' Your Own Competitor — Badly
hook: They gave you a free product and a script. You posted a 1-star review. The competitor lost 30% of sales.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone distrusts online reviews — this confirms the paranoia and triggers 'told you so' shares.
